title: Palantir Q1 2026 10-Q establishes AIP product and financial baseline

facts.text: Palantir's 10-Q describes AIP as providing third-party LLM connectivity, an agent and automation toolchain, end-user applications and an evaluation framework for production AI workflows.
facts.quote:
We have built four principal software platforms, Gotham, Foundry, Apollo, and our Artificial Intelligence Platform (“AIP”). 
Foundry is our foundational data operations platform, which provides the core capabilities for data management, logic 
authoring, systemic mapping development through our Ontology, analytics, and workflow development. AIP is our generative 
AI platform, which provides secure connectivity to third-party-provided large language models (“LLMs”), a development 
toolchain for building AI-powered agents and automations, an array of AI-enabled end user applications, a broad evaluations 
framework for governing AI workflows in production, and more.

facts.text: For the quarter ended March 31, 2026, Palantir reported $1.6 billion of revenue, 85% year-over-year growth and an 87% gross margin.
facts.quote:
For the three months ended March 31, 2026, we generated $1.6 billion in revenue, reflecting a 85% growth rate from the three 
months ended March 31, 2025, when we generated $0.9 billion in revenue. 
In the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, we generated income from operations of $754 million and $176 million, 
respectively, or adjusted income from operations of $984 million and  $391 million, respectively, when excluding stock-based 
compensation and related employer payroll taxes.  
In the three months ended March 31, 2026  and 2025, our gross profit was $1.4 billion and $0.7 billion, respectively, reflecting 
a gross margin of 87% and 80%, respectively, or 88% and 82%, respectively, when excluding stock-based compensation.

facts.text: Palantir reported 1,007 customers for the period ended March 31, 2026, compared with 769 for the prior-year period.
facts.quote:
We define a customer as an organization from which we have recognized revenue during the trailing twelve-month period. 
During the period ended March 31, 2026  and 2025, we had 1,007 and 769 customers, respectively, including companies in 
various commercial sectors and government agencies around the world.

facts.text: Palantir reported average trailing-twelve-month revenue of $108 million for its top twenty customers, up 55%, and said it conducts some pilots and bootcamps at its own expense without guaranteed returns.
facts.quote:
We have built lasting and significant customer relationships and partnerships with some of the world’s leading government 
institutions and companies. Our average revenue for the top twenty customers during the trailing twelve months ended March 
31, 2026 was $108 million, which grew 55% from an average of $70 million in revenue from the top twenty customers during 
the trailing twelve months ended March 31, 2025, demonstrating our expanding relationships with existing customers. 
Organizations in the commercial and government sectors face similar challenges when it comes to managing data, and we 
intend to expand our reach in both markets moving forward. Our decisions about which customer relationships require further 
investment may change over time, based on our assessment of the potential long-term value that our software can generate for 
them. We conduct pilots and bootcamps with customers, generally at our own expense and without a guarantee of future 
returns, in order to access a unique set of opportunities that others may pass over for lack of resources and shorter investment 
horizons.

facts.text: Palantir lists long sales cycles, customer concentration, possible failure to deploy new AI technologies, platform implementation complexity and intense competition among its risk factors.

inferences: The filing places agent tooling and evaluation inside a broader data, ontology and deployment platform rather than presenting AIP as a standalone model product.
Strong company-wide growth and margins coexist with customer concentration and self-funded deployment effort, so company-level results cannot be assigned to AIP without segment or product disclosure.
research_judgment: The 10-Q supplies an authoritative company-wide operating baseline and confirms how management defines AIP and Ontology. It does not disclose AIP revenue, Agent usage, deployment conversion or product-level margins; those omissions prevent attributing the reported financial growth to Agent adoption.

thesis_impacts.explanation: The filing confirms that Palantir integrates models, data, Ontology, agent tooling and evaluation, but does not establish that these elements create durable pricing power.
Customer growth and concentration provide an incumbent distribution baseline, while self-funded pilots and long sales cycles qualify the economics of expansion.

alternative_explanations: The reported growth may be driven by government contracts or non-Agent platform demand rather than AIP.
AIP adoption may accelerate customer expansion but require enough deployment support to limit incremental margins.
unknowns: AIP-specific revenue, bookings, customer count, retention and gross margin are not disclosed.
The conversion rate and cost of pilots or bootcamps are not disclosed.
The filing does not quantify production Agent tasks or business outcomes.
follow_up_indicators: Track AIP-specific commercial metrics in earnings calls and future filings.
Track customer concentration, professional-services intensity and pilot conversion.
Seek independent customer evidence separating AIP outcomes from broader Palantir deployments.
